name: Nggwahyi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Volume II ("Biu-Mandara"). Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 24. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. 199 pp. Ngwaxi list pp. 78 ff. — as digitised in Lexibank CLDF dataset 'kraftchadic' v4.1 (Tresoldi, List, Cysouw, Bouda; doi:10.5281/zenodo.13832124)
sources.note: Wordlist data only: 428 Ngwaxi forms, 321 of them carrying a grave (low-tone) diacritic, 5 a circumflex, none an acute — i.e. Kraft's transcription is tone-marked; no stress is marked and the CLDF dataset carries none of Kraft's cover-page/phonology notes.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation — entry 'Nggwahyi'
sources.note: Would confirm identity (one village, Askira-Uba LGA; possible dialect-of-Bura status) and list any unpublished wordlists or notes on the language; site is captcha-protected to non-browser downloads.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT. pp. 51, 153
sources.note: Nothing on Nggwahyi stress or tone; p. 51 places Nggwahyi in the Bura sub-group of the Margi group (after Hoffmann 1988); p. 153 states 'Data is only available for Bura and the three Margi subgroup languages' — i.e. Gravina had no Nggwahyi data at all.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (ed.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Nggwahyi (data supplied by Charles H. Kraft, 18 July 2007). MPI-EVA Leipzig
sources.note: Numerals 1-1000 only, tone-marked (e.g. tə̀ŋ '1', sɪɗà '2', makùr̃ '3'); no statement on stress or tone; notes 'a decimal system' and ~2,000 speakers.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid nggw1242 (HTML and) and reference record 66904 (Kraft 1981 II)
sources.note: Zero descriptive references; most extensive description = Kraft 1981 wordlist ('a wordlist or less'); only other refs are Hoffmann 1988 (classification overview) and Ethnologue 16. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Volume I ("Plateau-Sahel"). MSAA A 23. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Introduction (front matter, scan pages k-03/k-04)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; it says each language entry (hence the Ngwaxi entry in vol. II) 'consists of a cover page giving information concerning the elicitation and analysis, a tentative phonemic inventory, several pages of notes on the phonology and six pages of the word lists', and that transcriptions are 'at best.. semi-phonemic'. the scan we hold stops at the table of contents; the Ngwaxi entry itself is not yet obtained.

sources.citation: Lexibank variety page 'Ngwaxi' (kraftchadic) and kraftchadic README, lexibank.clld.org / github.com/lexibank/kraftchadic
sources.note: Segment inventory computed from Kraft's forms; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Nggwahyi language' and 'Biu–Mandara languages'; Wikidata Q56265; ISO 639-3 page ngx
sources.note: Nothing; the Biu-Mandara page (citing Blench 2019 Atlas) gives location 'One village, Borno State, Askira-Uba LGA'; Wikipedia cites only Ethnologue 18 and the ELCat report.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2013. The Chadic Language Family: Classification and Name Index. Mega-Chad Research Network / IU ScholarWorks
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Authoritative name index (Nggwahyi = Ngwaxi = Ngwohi) and any listed sources; no stress content expected.

sources.citation: Hoffmann, Carl F. 1988. Towards an internal classification of the languages of the Bura-Margyi group. In D. Barreteau & H. Tourneux (eds.), Le milieu et les hommes: recherches comparatives et historiques dans le bassin du lac Tchad (Actes du 2e colloque Méga-Tchad, ORSTOM Bondy, 3-4 oct. 1985), 253-263. Paris: ORSTOM
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other Nggwahyi-linked reference in Glottolog; uses Hoffmann's own Bura-group data and may carry tonal/prosodic remarks on the West Margi (Bura, Nggwahyi, Cibak, Putai) subgroup. ORSTOM colloquia are usually open on IRD Horizon but no record was found by search.

tone.summary: Says nothing about tone; a subgrouping paper on the Bura-Margyi group that cites Nggwahyi pronouns and about twenty words, printed without tone marks.
tone.citation_as_reported: Hoffmann, Carl F. 1988. Towards an internal classification of the languages of the Bura-Margyi group. In Daniel Barreteau & Henry Tourneux (eds.), Le milieu et les hommes: recherches comparatives et historiques dans le bassin du lac Tchad. Actes du 2eme colloque Mega-Tchad, ORSTOM Bondy, 3-4 octobre 1985 (Colloques et Seminaires), 253-263. Paris: ORSTOM.

sources.citation: Hoffmann, Carl. 1963. A Grammar of the Margi Language. London: Oxford University Press for IAI
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (archive.org lending); also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.180) (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Closest well-described relative (Margi sub-group of the same Margi group); documents the tonal system typical of the group, useful only as a family proxy, not a Nggwahyi statement.

sources.citation: Searches with no result: Glottolog reference search, IA Scholar, archive.
sources.note: No phonology article, thesis, JIPA illustration, SIL or LINCOM description of Nggwahyi/Ngwaxi surfaced under any name.
